rules.sentence: If the radial nerve is entrapped and symptoms last for several months, surgery is indicated to relieve the pressure on the nerve.
Sometimes, it is difficult to distinguish radial neuropathies from central nervous system (CNS) lesions, as they can both cause wrist extension weakness (wrist drop).
To differentiate between a peripheral radial neuropathy from a central pathology, test the brachioradialis muscle.
It is always weak in a peripheral radial nerve injury and less affected with a CNS disorder.
The majority (up to 92%) resolve with observation alone for 3 to 4 months in the setting of injuries or fractures to the humerus.
